summary: Service-bot RBAC rehydration failing after Okta group rename; internal analytics access degraded
description: Issue summary: After a planned Okta group rename for the analytics team, the internal analytics-runner service-bot stopped receiving updated RBAC claims. Impact: intermittent 403s for analyst dashboards, failing nightly model observability jobs that rely on the service-bot token, and elevated support noise. Environment: prod-us-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a new session for analytics-runner service-bot (token refresh or new login). 2) Inspect RBAC claim payload via /internal/debug/claims endpoint. 3) Observe stale group list and missing role assignments. Observed logs: identity-proxy logs show SCIM delta events processed, but rbac-cache rehydration job logs show "no eligible mapping" and many 409 duplicate-upsert errors. Hypothesis: Okta group rename produced a short SCIM backlog + a small number of duplicate membership deltas; the cache rehydration worker treats a duplicate-upsert as a hard-failure and aborts processing for that tenant, leaving service-bot claims stale. Temporary mitigation: forced full re-sync for affected tenant and manual membership normalization script. Resolution: applied migration to normalize group IDs and retriggered rehydration; patched worker to tolerate idempotent duplicate-upsert and added a backoff-retry for transient DB conflicts. Follow-up: add monitoring for rehydration abort rate and a guardrail to auto-trigger full-resync when processing failure rate > 5% in a 10m window.
investigation_notes: 03/11 09:12 - Initial alert: SRE oncall observed surge in 403s for /internal/analytics endpoint (pager triggered).
03/11 09:35 - Support confirmed customer-facing dashboards are unaffected; internal analyst workflows impacted. Noted recent Okta group rename rollout at 03/10 22:00 via #identity-ops slack thread.
03/11 10:05 - Pulled identity-proxy and scim-sync logs: SCIM processed group rename events but delta entries included duplicate membership->upsert pairs for ~120 users.
03/11 11:00 - Rehydration worker aborted on first duplicate-upsert DB conflict; code path lacked retry and bubbled abort to the tenant queue.
03/12 02:15 - Ran manual normalization script to collapse duplicate membership deltas and queued a forced full resync for affected tenant.
03/12 03:30 - Observed analytics-runner service-bot claim shows expected groups and 403 rate decreased to baseline.
03/12 10:00 - Deployed patch to rehydration worker (idempotent upsert + 5 retry attempts with exponential backoff) and added instrumentation around abort counts.
03/13 08:00 - Verified no regressions during a subsequent staged Okta group rename in staging environment.
Postmortem action items: update SCIM rollout checklist, add preflight check to detect duplicate deltas, and add runbook step to force resync when rehydration aborts >5% within 10m.
resolution: Patched rehydration worker to handle idempotent duplicate-upsert; ran normalization and forced full SCIM resync for affected tenant; monitored and validated 48h without regression.
resolution_notes: Applied DB migration to normalize group identifiers at 03/12 02:10 UTC.
Forced full SCIM sync at 03/12 02:20 UTC (background job ID: sync-20260312-01).
Deployed worker patch in canary on 03/12 10:00 UTC and to prod on 03/12 10:15 UTC (PR-442).
